# XTF fixtures

`ModernSRGB.xtf` was generated by macOS AppKit using
`Tools/generate-srgb-xtf-fixture.swift`. Each of its seven colors is a real
`NSKeyedArchiver` archive of `NSColor(srgbRed:green:blue:alpha:)`. The generator
removes the embedded system ICC data and its `NSICC` reference, retaining the
standard sRGB `NSID = 7` identity. AppKit unarchives each resulting color and
verifies that converting it to sRGB returns the original channels. The archived
alpha is deliberately different from the outer XTF transparency.

The system profile is not redistributed here. For a full-profile check, generate
both variants on macOS, then run the `xtf` Rust integration test on Linux with
`XRG_TEST_APPKIT_SRGB` pointing to the generated `ModernSRGB-full.xtf`. This also
checks that changing one profile byte makes the importer reject it. The known
3,144-byte sRGB IEC61966-2.1 profile has BLAKE3 fingerprint
`584d7f5ba6f0afe67a1bba04b2a12d5e336e9721b198d6c98ee20b1a6e5759fc`.
Unknown profiles are rejected even when their archive claims `NSID = 7`.

The original application's `ClassicTheme.xtf` remains in
`XRGTests/Fixtures/ClassicTheme.xtf` and is tested against the shared Classic
preset. These tests establish archive/component handling, not matching across
physical monitors and display profiles.
